paras: The Birmingham police shooting of Albert Brown was a gunfight in Birmingham, Alabama, in March 1919, in which two policemen fired on two Black soldiers and Brown, one of the soldiers, shot both officers before he was killed. Policemen W. D. Evans and A. W. Phillips died of their wounds a few hours later, and the other soldier escaped. Black newspapers carried it as a case of officers firing on soldiers 'without cause'.

According to a dispatch dated Birmingham, March 18, the shooting took place 'a few nights ago', when the officers accosted the two soldiers as they came out of a 'lonely street'. The policemen demanded to know what was in a suit case the soldiers were carrying, and when the men were 'slow to reply' they opened fire. Brown was killed, but not before he had mortally wounded both officers, and his companion got away.
No report of an inquest, of a search for the escaped soldier, or of any arrest appears in the coverage.

The story reached the Black press as a Blade News Service item, printed on March 22, 1919, by the Wisconsin Weekly Blade under the headline 'Colored Soldier Kills Two Policemen' and by the Phoenix Tribune on its front page. Both versions placed the blame on the police, closing with the observation that 'indiscretion by officers' in arresting Black people, 'and especially soldiers', had already cost many officers their lives. The Phoenix Tribune's text went further, saying the two officers had long been on the force and that their records 'in dealing with Negroes are not at all complimentary'. It ended with a warning that police 'will soon learn down here' to deal with Black men 'in a more civil manner, but perhaps too late'.

The dispatch contradicts itself on the soldiers' fate: it first says Brown fired after the officers 'shot and killed his friend', then that the officers killed Brown and that 'the other man in uniform escaped'. With only two soldiers described, the later account, in which Brown died and his companion escaped, reads more consistently.

reader.title: Birmingham police shooting of Albert Brown
bases: Two Birmingham policemen stopped two Black soldiers on a street and opened fire on them, killing one, and were themselves fatally shot (A1, A2).
Both reports are the same Blade News Service text (A2 is credited to it, A1 reprints it nearly word for word), so there is one source; no independent or local report was found.

accounts.label: Blade News Service dispatch
accounts.gist: The officers stopped two soldiers over a suit case and fired on them without cause when they were slow to answer; Brown mortally wounded both officers before he was killed, and the other soldier escaped.

framing.detail: The Phoenix Tribune carried the dispatch whole, adding that the officers' records with Black people were 'not at all complimentary' and that police would learn to deal with Black men 'in a more civil manner, but perhaps too late'.
The Wisconsin Weekly Blade headlined it 'Colored Soldier Kills Two Policemen' and closed on officers' 'indiscretion' in arresting Black people and soldiers.

versions.value: The officers 'shot and killed his friend' (Brown's companion) before Brown fired
The officers killed Brown, and 'the other man in uniform escaped'

conflicts.note: The contradiction is inside the single dispatch both papers printed; with only two soldiers present, the later, more detailed sentences (Brown killed, companion escaped) are the more coherent reading, but the text does not settle it.

sources.note: Birmingham, March 18 dispatch: officers Evans and Phillips killed by soldier Albert Brown after shooting 'without cause'; adds comment on the officers' records and a closing warning; printed under a headline belonging to the column.
quotes: Policemen W. D. Evans and A. W. Phillips were both shot and killed by Albert Brown, a Negro soldier, after the officers had without cause shot and killed his friend.
Offeeers Evans and Phillips have long been on the force and their records in dealing with Negroes are not at all complimentary.
They will soon learn down here that a very different kind of nigger must be dealt with and in a more civil manner, but perhaps too late.

sources.note: Blade News Service version of the same text, headlined 'Colored Soldier Kills Two Policemen'; omits the Tribune's last two sentences and says 'colored' for 'Negro'.
quotes: the men in uniform being slow to reply the policemen opened fire on them, killing Brown but not before they were mortally wounded
Indiscretion by officers in making or attempting to make arrests of colored people and especially soldiers, have already caused many of them their lives.
